headline.text: In Keski-Suomi, the crude MDT-recorded share is 3.8% (95% CI 2.5–5.5; n=24/637), whose 95% confidence interval excludes the national 6.0% (893/14873), though MDT records measure recording practice, not care.

details.text: Across overlapping treatment categories, the 95% confidence intervals include the national values for Keski-Suomi's crude curative share of 27.2% (95% CI 23.9–30.7; n=173/637) vs 27.0% (4009/14873) and crude symptomatic share of 36.3% (95% CI 32.6–40.1; n=231/637) vs 39.5% (5871/14873), whereas the crude life-prolonging share of 37.2% (95% CI 33.5–41.0; n=237/637) excludes the national 30.4% (4522/14873).

Although Keski-Suomi's regional pathway document states that every new case is reviewed in an MDT, specialised care procedures are entered into HILMO only from direct patient contacts, so the crude 3.8% (95% CI 2.5–5.5; n=24/637) MDT share reflects recording practice rather than care.

Keski-Suomi's regional pathway document handles referrals as quickly as possible with no time stated, targets a lung clinic appointment within 2–3 weeks or at the latest about 1 month and tissue sample results in about 1–2 weeks, names occupational health as a referral source, and names no diagnostic contact person, without reporting whether target times are met.

Nationally, preliminary unpublished study figures show the average time from symptoms to treatment is 155 days in Finland compared with 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark, with 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care as the longest stage.

headline.text: Registry diagnosis concordance is about 90%, but county treatment shares are crude, unadjusted for age or stage, and public data omit key pathway dates and pre-referral steps.

details.text: County shares are crude and not age-adjusted; age-adjusted values exist only from Kuva 16 for curative treatment by sex, digitised from a figure at about ±0.5 percentage points precision (national lines 26.7% for men, 26.9% for women), while Keski-Suomi's crude curative 27.2% (95% CI 23.9–30.7; n=173/637) shows no gap vs the national 27.0% (4009/14873).

As a separate limitation from age adjustment, county shares cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients, while a journal article found that HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, concerning diagnosis concordance only.

Keski-Suomi's crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 24.5% (95% CI 21.3–28.0; n=156/637), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 27.5% (4089/14873) and is not distinguishable from it, and this category mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded.

Public data do not measure symptoms or referral dates, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, imaging appears only where diagnosis rests on clinical examination alone in approximately 20% of patients, and although 93.6% have a specialist visit within 12 months, visit and treatment start dates are not reported.

headline.text: The team recommends that Keski-Suomi publish stage, drug, and MDT recording completeness, report access times using THL 21/2016 definitions with handover alerts, and standardise referrals and diagnostic coordination.

details.text: With Keski-Suomi's crude 3.8% (95% CI 2.5–5.5; n=24/637) MDT-recorded share despite its pathway document reviewing every new case, stage missing for about 48% of patients, and incomplete national data, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding while the STM roadmap (measure 3.2.1) plans a national quality registry with its decree updated by 2026–2028.

Since the Health Care Act (§52) sets no maximum time for a cancer suspicion and Keski-Suomi's pathway document does not monitor its targets, the team recommends reporting access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers with handover alerts, while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with referral criteria and time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Since mentor insight notes a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating and Keski-Suomi's pathway document states no referral time and names no diagnostic contact, the team recommends a KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule after a normal X-ray, and a named diagnostic contact, while the STM roadmap (measure 1.2.3) plans care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 for county adoption by 2029–2031.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
